notes.note: You can now fill forms faster in Smart Window. When clicking into a form field or selecting *Fill* from sources, Smart Window will now suggest data to use based on your relevant open tabs and saved autofill data.
New Tab now keeps a library of custom wallpapers under *Your images*, rather than only the most recent one.

Added support for the [`navigate`][1] option for the `Notification` constructor and `ServiceWorkerRegistration.showNotification()`, which specifies a URL to navigate to when the notification is clicked.


  [1]: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Notification/navigate

The [WebAuthn conditional UI][1] will now be shown on input elements with an `autocomplete="webauthn"` attribute. Previously, the UI would only be shown on input elements with additional autofill field values, e.g. `autocomplete="username webauthn"`.
([Learn more][2])


  [1]: https://github.com/w3c/webauthn/blob/main/explainers/conditional-ui.md
  [2]: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#autofill-processing-model

Firefox now supports the `cache` value for [`PerformanceResourceTiming.deliveryType`][1], allowing websites to identify resources served from the HTTP cache.


  [1]: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/PerformanceResourceTiming/deliveryType

Firefox now supports [typed arithmetic][1] in CSS `calc()`, allowing units to be multiplied and divided within math functions.


  [1]: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Values_and_units/Using_typed_arithmetic
Fixed an issue where the Network Monitor could miss WebSocket messages if they arrived immediately after a connection was established.

Menus such as the *List all tabs* menu, the *Settings* menu, and *Unified Search* menu are now visually consistent on Windows with a High Contrast theme. The user is now able to customize menu background color and text color when creating a custom theme in Windows Settings by setting Background and Text, respectively.
PDF generation (for saving as PDF and also printing on Linux and macOS) now uses SkPDF. This allows PDFs to be more accessible, and also fixes a variety of PDF rendering issues.

system_requirements:
## Windows

### Operating Systems (32-bit and 64-bit)
 - Windows 10 or later

### Recommended Hardware
-  1 gigahertz (GHz) or faster compatible processor or System on a Chip (SoC)
-  1GB of RAM / 2GB of RAM for the 64-bit version
-  500MB of hard drive space

---

## Mac

### Operating Systems
- macOS 10.15 or later

### Recommended Hardware
- Macintosh computer with an Intel x86 or Apple silicon processor
- 512 MB of RAM
- 200 MB hard drive space

---

## GNU/Linux

### Software Requirements

*Please note that GNU/Linux distributors may provide packages for your distribution which have different requirements.*

- Firefox will not run at all without the following libraries or packages:
    - glibc 2.17 or higher (2.28 or higher on arm64)
    - GTK+ 3.14 or higher
    - libglib 2.42 or higher
    - libstdc++ 4.8.1 or higher (6.0 or higher on arm64)
    - X.Org 1.0 or higher (1.7 or higher is recommended)
- For optimal functionality, we recommend the following libraries or packages:
    - DBus 1.0 or higher
    - NetworkManager 0.7 or higher
    - PulseAudio

Firefox Beta gets updated 3 times a week and as a consequence, the release notes for the Beta channel are updated continuously to reflect features that have reached sufficient maturity to benefit from community feedback and bug reports.
Warning: Features listed here may or may not make a final release of Firefox

In addition to these release notes, you can follow ongoing development via the [Firefox Trains][1] website or our [@FirefoxBeta][2] Bluesky account. [1]: https://whattrainisitnow.com/beta/ [2]: https://bsky.app/profile/firefoxbeta.bsky.social
